quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Osaka Cement annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): net sales JPY 223,686 million (+1.9% year on year, higher sales in Cement, New Materials and others), operating income JPY 13,648 million (prior year JPY 9,351 million), ordinary income JPY 14,405 million (+JPY 5,038 million), net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 11,214 million (+JPY 2,205 million, after an impairment loss on fixed assets). By segment: Cement net sales JPY 158,799 million (+1.5%) and operating income JPY 5,495 million (+526.0%), as domestic price hikes to cover cost increases offset lower domestic volume; Mineral Products JPY 17,505 million (+0.8%), operating income JPY 2,986 million (-5.2%); Construction Materials JPY 23,020 million (-2.4%), operating income JPY 1,480 million (-19.5%); Optoelectronics net sales JPY 2,732 million (+8.9%) on higher sales volume of optical measuring instruments, with an operating loss of JPY 56 million, an improvement of JPY 298 million on cost reductions in optical communications components; New Materials net sales JPY 18,074 million (+15.3%) and operating income JPY 2,479 million (+9.5%), driven by the product mix of electronic materials for semiconductor manufacturing equipment; Other JPY 3,553 million (-8.3%). No customer accounted for 10% or more of total sales, so no major customer is disclosed.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 223,686 million (+1.9%); operating income JPY 13,648 million; Optoelectronics net sales JPY 2,732 million (+8.9%), operating loss JPY 56 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Osaka Cement annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Production, orders and volumes, fiscal year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): production by segment (manufacturing-cost basis) totalled JPY 120,714 million (97.5% of the prior year), including Optoelectronics JPY 1,733 million (106.6%) and New Materials JPY 14,042 million (107.5%); orders received JPY 19,279 million (120.3%) with an order backlog of JPY 3,595 million (90.7%), covering construction works in Construction Materials (orders JPY 18,857 million, backlog JPY 3,555 million) and software in Other (other segments mostly do not produce to order). Japan's domestic cement demand fell 6.5% to 30,532 thousand tonnes while exports rose 7.1%; the company's own cement sales were 6,971 thousand tonnes domestic and 1,375 thousand tonnes export (8,346 thousand tonnes in total).
quarterly_data.figure: Production JPY 120,714 million; Optoelectronics production JPY 1,733 million; order backlog JPY 3,595 million; company cement sales 8,346 thousand tonnes

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Osaka Cement annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D, fiscal year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): Optoelectronics R&D spending was JPY 703 million; the year's main results were the commercialization of coherent-capable LN (lithium niobate) modulators for 1.2Tbps/1.6Tbps transmission systems, and development of element technologies for next-generation compact optical device elements. The New Technology Research Laboratories do the basic research and product development, and the Optoelectronics Division commercializes the applied products.
quarterly_data.figure: Optoelectronics R&D JPY 703 million; 1.2Tbps/1.6Tbps coherent LN modulators commercialized

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Osaka Cement annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D, fiscal year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): group R&D spending was JPY 3,559 million, of which New Materials JPY 1,757 million, Cement JPY 896 million and Construction Materials JPY 202 million. New Materials results: commercialization and application expansion of electrostatic chucks for next-generation semiconductor equipment; development of differentiated materials technology and a low-cost process technology for the electrostatic chuck generation after next; mass-production process technology for cosmetic materials and base technology for functional materials.
quarterly_data.figure: Group R&D JPY 3,559 million; New Materials R&D JPY 1,757 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Osaka Cement annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capex and new-facility plans (annual securities report): capital expenditure in the fiscal year ended March 2026 totalled JPY 31,544 million: Cement JPY 16,158 million, Mineral Products JPY 5,395 million, Construction Materials JPY 397 million, Optoelectronics JPY 234 million, New Materials JPY 8,787 million, Other JPY 571 million. Planned new facilities as of the year end: New Materials Division (Ichikawa City, Chiba) capacity increase for electronic materials for semiconductor manufacturing equipment (construction of a new manufacturing building etc.), total JPY 13,105 million, JPY 11,898 million already paid, started July 2023, completion planned March 2027; Akiyoshi Mining shipping berth renewal and extension (Mine City, Yamaguchi), JPY 6,189 million (JPY 5,640 million paid), completion August 2026; Gifu Plant No. 2 kiln exhaust-gas treatment renewal, JPY 1,296 million, completion September 2027; Shibaura service station and Tokyo SOC Shibaura plant renovation, JPY 3,823 million, completion September 2027; Naoetsu Port service station storage and shipping facilities (Joetsu City, Niigata), JPY 2,791 million, completion January 2028; a 13,000-tonne limestone carrier for SOC Marine, JPY 3,640 million, May 2026 to March 2029. No significant disposal or sale is planned.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 31,544 million (Optoelectronics JPY 234 million, New Materials JPY 8,787 million); electronic materials new building JPY 13,105 million, completion March 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Osaka Cement annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management's review of the 2023-25 Medium-Term Management Plan (annual securities report): under the plan the company developed next-generation optical communications components to gain share and improve profitability, increased production capacity for electronic materials for semiconductor manufacturing equipment (including the new manufacturing building) and developed electronic materials for next-generation equipment, and expanded its Australian business and invested in a Philippine cement company. Domestic cement demand was weaker than initially assumed and labour shortages, faster inflation and higher material costs held back margins in Cement, while the High-Performance Products business fell short of the initial plan because the recovery in sales volume was delayed; ROE was 5.8% and ROIC 3.3%. Company outlook: public-sector cement demand is expected to be flat year on year (Noto earthquake reconstruction) and private demand to decline on labour shortages and rising construction costs, so domestic cement demand is expected to decrease.
